text.p: Olympic Financial Ltd may be worth $25-$30 per share, analysts said, noting that heavy volume in its shares Monday came on acquisition speculation.
Shares in the auto finance concern were up 5-5/8 to 23-1/4 on 1.6 million shares traded after the Minneapolis-based concern said it had received an expression of interest from a possible acquirer.
That volume was triple normal levels, analysts said.
Acquirers could include other finance firms, such as General Electric's GE Capital, or regional banks, such as Norwest Corp or KeyCorp, analysts said.
The company could not be reached for comment, but a secretary confirmed a conference call for analysts has been scheduled for 0315 CDT.
In a statement Monday morning, Olympic announced the expression of interest and said the chairman, president and chief executive Jeffrey Mack had resigned.

"My guess is an offer came in for the company, or some expression of interest, and Mack said, 'This is my company and I'm not going to sell.' The board probably reacted by saying, 'That's for us to say,'" said Principal Financial analyst Bob Ollech.
At $25-$30 per share, Olympic Financial would be worth $500-$600 million, analysts said.

The company said it is the largest independent provider of auto financing. It said it buys, sells and services auto loans through 17 regional buying centers in 14 states. It also said it has expanded its dealer network to include dealers in 38 states.
